title: Relay strategy service-key rotation policy decision
observed_behavior_before: The relay strategy plan already scoped Items 3 and 5 to service-authored publication by the configured Bahia service key.

Existing discovery design and client configuration support trusted service pubkey lists for accepting discovery during rotation windows, but repository evidence did not identify an implementation requirement to build multi-key publication rotation before relay strategy Items 3 or 5.
Backend discovery projection signs ContextVM discovery, NIP-51 relay sets, and advisory NIP-65 relay preferences through the configured projector signer, not through a multi-signer rotation workflow.
intended_behavior: Relay strategy Items 3 and 5 remain scoped to a single configured Bahia service signing key.

Clients continue validating discovery and relay strategy events against their configured trusted service pubkey list, so operators can configure a transition trust window without requiring dual-publish implementation in this relay-strategy slice.

A dedicated key-management Bead is required only if a future deployment needs automatic multi-key publication rotation, signer orchestration, or dual-publish lifecycle management beyond the configured service key.

rationale: docs/plans/relay-strategy-2026-06-06.md records the single-key scope and says multi-key rotation must be separate if needed.

docs/designs/nostr-native-system-discovery.md supports trusted service pubkey lists for client-side rotation acceptance, which satisfies the discovery trust boundary without changing Items 3 or 5 publication semantics.
internal/adapters/nostr/projector.go publishes relay-set and NIP-65 events through the configured projector signer, preserving the existing service-key authorship model.

included: Decision closeout for relay strategy service-key rotation policy
excluded: Changes to web Nostr helper modules
Changes to relay-set or NIP-65 projection code
